sourceCoverage.rationale: The public original 60:49 interview has nine creator chapters, 1,823 time-indexed caption entries, and thirteen bounded claims distributed across its full argument, with explicit automatic-caption uncertainty.

supportingArgument.rationale: The Reader tests whether affordable intelligence can expand the scope of accepted, safe work instead of treating a vendor price ratio or speculative occupational displacement as established.

evidenceRoles.rationale: The source distinguishes creator quotations and forecasts, Particle commercial benchmarks, Stanford historical unit prices, METR randomized productivity research, and non-empirical conceptual companions.

counterargument.rationale: The analysis gives substantive competing views about uneven capability, governance and institutional permissions, productivity measurement bias, market concentration and inequitable opportunity.

tradeoffs.rationale: The proposed design compares token price, retries, accepted outcomes, human verification, provenance, security controls, recovery cost, and practical project scale under controlled workloads.

falsifiability.rationale: A proposed paired three-workload evaluation would compare premium and inexpensive model routing with task acceptance tests, blinded review where possible and full accounting of verification and retries.

originalSynthesis.rationale: The distinct editorial finding is that reduced execution cost matters only when individuals can complete larger useful projects under fixed source, quality, safety and authorization conditions.

performance.rationale: Quantitative metrics are clearly scoped: the thirty-fold speaker comparison is anecdotal, Particle benchmarks are vendor-reported with a 95 percent cache assumption, and no independent model experiment was run.

economics.rationale: The article correctly divides total model/tool charges, human verification and amortized overhead over independently accepted jobs and distinguishes that from token usage and vendor per-task estimates.

threatGovernance.rationale: The article requires bounded agent execution, trustworthy source paths, auditable version custody, explicit permission for destructive or external changes, and rollback rather than self-approved release.
